page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7a.16xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with a dedicated AMD EPYC 7T83 processor running at 2.55 GHz. The instance is configured with 64 vCPUs, derived from 32 physical cores with 2 threads per core, and is paired with 256.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, relying instead on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 16 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core processing capabilities, with stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and PassMark CPU scores placing in the top 25%. The AMD EPYC processor demonstrates high efficiency in parallelized workloads, as evidenced by strong results in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, software compilation with Clang, ray tracing, and image processing. Cryptographic operations are highly optimized, supported by hardware-accelerated AES and SHA instruction sets. However, single-threaded performance and large-block memory bandwidth operations fall into the average tier, representing a potential bottleneck for memory-bound sequential tasks.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.g7a.16xlarge offers high resource density for enterprise applications that require dedicated CPU allocation without the added cost of bundled local storage. It is highly suitable for database operations, as demonstrated by strong PassMark database and Redis SET performance, as well as medium-scale LLM inference and parallelized build systems. The lack of local storage means workloads requiring high-speed local caching must utilize network storage, which may impact overall I/O latency.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7a.16xlarge is a general-purpose, KVM-hypervised instance featuring a dedicated AMD EPYC 7T83 processor with 64 vCPUs and 256.0 GB of RAM. Operating on an x86_64 architecture at 2.55 GHz, it delivers a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The instance does not include local storage or GPUs, relying on a 16 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmark results show strong multi-core CPU performance, database operations, and Redis throughput, though single-threaded tasks and large-block memory bandwidth remain in the average tier. This profile makes the instance highly efficient for multi-threaded enterprise workloads, database hosting, and software compilation, offering a solid balance of compute and memory resources.
